question_text: A 76-year-old man presents for a follow-up appointment at his primary care provider’s office. The patient has severe osteoarthritis, which substantially limits his daily physical activity. Several imaging studies have confirmed severe articular degeneration and evidence of bone grinding on bone in his hip joints. The patient suffers from chronic pain and depression that have been resistant to medication. At the physician’s office, his blood pressure is 119/67 mm Hg, the respirations are 18/min, the pulse is 87/min, and the temperature is 36.7°C (98.0°F). On physical examination, the patient has a flat affect and appears anxious. He has significant pain and limited passive and active range of motion of his hip joints bilaterally. This patient would most likely benefit from which of the following procedures if there are no contraindications?
